SmarType UX Review
UX review · SmarType 0.12.0-beta012 (versionCode 138)

SmarType end-to-end UX review

A walkthrough of every main flow, from first launch to AI rewrite, on an Android emulator and on a real Galaxy S22 Ultra with Premium. Each finding has the screen, what goes wrong for the user, and a proposed fix. No app code was changed.

25 Oct 2026Play beta build, same code as main @ c3d86d39cEmulator: Pixel, Android 16 · Phone: SM-S908E, Android 16
14High: blocks or misleads users
23Medium: friction or confusion
10Low: polish
47Findings in total

Fix these first

  1. AI rewrite can fail silently (A2): the panel closed and the text stayed the same, with no error. Users will think the AI does nothing.
  2. Error messages blame the user and use internal words (H1, A1, P1): "Update SmarType", "verification token", "billing catalog", "Sign in" shown to a signed-in user.
  3. Setup order (O3, O4): sign-in comes before the keyboard works, then a "Sign in before restoring" message appears right after signing in.
  4. No undo after Replace (A5): AI text replaces the user's text with no visible way back.
  5. Keyboard panels may be invisible to TalkBack (A8): needs a quick check with a screen reader.
  6. Back from the AI panel closes the keyboard (A9), and the panel's own back button looks like Enter (A10).
  7. Adding a language removes English and the globe key leaves SmarType (L1, L2).
  8. The mic hands users to another keyboard and doesn't bring them back (D1).

Onboarding and setup

First launch to a working keyboard.

O1Medium

Intro pages are generic and mostly empty

What happens

Four pages of abstract icons and marketing lines ("the most intelligent and customizable keyboard"). Dots and "Page 2 of 4" say the same thing twice, and the lower half of each page is empty. Nothing shows what SmarType actually does differently.

Proposed fix

Cut to 2–3 pages that each show one real feature in motion: a suggestion appearing, a rewrite before/after, a theme switch. Remove the "Page X of 4" text and keep the dots.

O2Medium

Privacy page is a dense legal paragraph

What happens

One centred block names "third-party AI services", "Firebase or Google services", "account, profile, and subscription data". It reads like a policy, so users skip it, and it doesn't reassure about the one thing that matters: typed text.

Proposed fix

Three short lines with icons: "Typing stays on your phone" · "AI only sees text when you tap Rewrite or Translate" · "Your account uses Google sign-in". Link to the full privacy policy.

O3High

Sign-in comes before the keyboard works, with internal jargon

What happens

Right after onboarding the user must decide on sign-in before SmarType is even their keyboard. The screen repeats "Welcome to SmarType" (same as page 1), says sign-in is for "profile and account-backed features", and explains "Firebase Authentication and Firestore". There is no reason to sign in that a user would care about, such as free AI rewrites.

Proposed fix

Move sign-in after keyboard setup and a first try. Lead with the benefit ("Sign in to get free AI rewrites and keep Premium on all your phones"). Drop Firebase/Firestore from user-facing text; keep it in the privacy policy.

O4High

"Sign in before restoring or purchasing premium" appears right after signing in

What happens

The user has just signed in, and the first thing they see is a message telling them to sign in. There is also no confirmation that sign-in worked.

Proposed fix

Suppress the toast while sign-in is completing or just completed. Show a brief "Signed in as J…" confirmation instead.

O5Medium

Setup step 1 repeats the header text and shows a toggle that isn't one

What happens

The step 1 card's description is a copy of the header sentence ("This quick setup guides you through…"). The switch inside the card looks tappable but only reflects state; the real action is the button at the bottom. Users may try to flip it.

Proposed fix

Replace the switch with a status chip ("Not on yet" / "On ✓"). Description: "Android asks you to allow a new keyboard once." Put the action button inside the active step card.

Home

The hub after setup.

H1Highemulator

Plan card error blames the app version and still pushes Upgrade

What happens

"App verification failed. Update SmarType and try again." The user is already on the latest version, so updating won't help. The real cause is that Google Play couldn't confirm the device. The bright Upgrade button stays, but the subscription page then says plans are unavailable (P1).

Proposed fix

Map each verification failure to an accurate message and action (see sketch). Hide or disable Upgrade while plans can't load. Keep the internal reason in logs, not on screen.

H2Low

Premium card gives no details

What happens

"Premium · Active on this account" with no renewal date and no way to manage or cancel. Users who want to check billing have to go to Play Store on their own.

Proposed fix

Add the renewal date and a "Manage in Google Play" link.

H3Low

Home mixes main tasks with support links; AI Settings appears twice

What happens

Home lists Settings, AI Settings, Guides, Contact Support and Share as equal cards. AI Settings is also inside Settings. Nothing on Home lets the user try the keyboard or jump to the most-used items (themes, writing styles).

Proposed fix

Promote a "Try your keyboard" field and 2–3 shortcuts (Themes, Writing styles). Move Guides, Support and Share to a smaller group at the bottom.

Settings and themes

S1Medium

Help tip covers two settings rows

What happens

The first-visit tip for Smartbar floats over the next two rows, so Typing and Gestures can't be read or tapped until it's dismissed.

Proposed fix

Show tips as an inline banner under the row they describe, or anchor the bubble so it doesn't cover neighbours.

S2Medium

Typing rows have no descriptions; no settings search

What happens

Under "Typing and input", Keyboard, Smartbar, Typing and Gestures have no subtitles, while every other row has one. "Keyboard" and "Typing" are easy to confuse. Look and feel is split between Themes (keyboard) and App look (app). With this many settings, there is no search.

Proposed fix

Add one-line subtitles (e.g. Keyboard: "Height, number row, key sounds"; Typing: "Autocorrect, suggestions, capitalisation"). Add a search field at the top of Settings.

T1Low

Theme cards: menu button covers the preview, names cut off

What happens

The ⋮ button sits on top of the key preview. Names like "SmarType Day (Borderl…" are truncated. The Create theme tile takes a full card on its own row.

Proposed fix

Move ⋮ into the label row; allow two-line names. Make Create theme a smaller tile or a button in the top bar.

Keyboard

Typing in a neutral text box.

K1Mediumemulator

"teh" was not autocorrected to "the"

What happens

Typing "teh" then space left "teh", even though "the" appeared as a suggestion right after. If autocorrect is off by default, new users won't find out; if it's on, it didn't fire in a search field.

Proposed fix

Check the default. If off, offer it during setup. If it's skipped in search fields on purpose, that's fine; note it in the autocorrect flow doc.

K2Low

A suggestion chip shows a garbled two-line label

What happens

One suggestion shows "yesterday and" with "and" on a second line underneath, which looks broken.

Proposed fix

Keep suggestion chips to a single line and truncate long multi-word predictions.

K3Medium

Clipboard button opens a chooser instead of the clipboard

What happens

Tapping the clipboard icon shows two big tiles (Clipboard / Quick Notes), so pasting from history always takes an extra tap.

Proposed fix

Open the clipboard directly, with a Notes tab inside the panel.

K4Medium

More actions: Reorder button covers the grid; toolbar icons are unlabeled

What happens

The floating Reorder button sits on top of the second row of actions. In the toolbar, some icons (four-way arrows, dotted square) don't say what they do.

Proposed fix

Put Reorder in the panel header. Add labels on long-press and in the More actions grid, and use clearer icons for cursor control and select.

K5Medium

First tap on the AI button is sometimes ignored

What happens

On the phone, right after typing a word, the first tap on the AI sparkle showed a pressed state but didn't open the panel; the second tap did.

Proposed fix

Make sure a tap while a word is still being composed opens the panel on the first try.

AI rewrite and translate

Tested on the phone with Premium, plus the error states on the emulator.

A1Highemulator

Unavailable state repeats the error three times and leaves Rewrite looking active

What happens

"Unavailable", "App verification failed" (twice) and "Managed AI requires a valid app verification token" all on one panel. In the AI tab the big gradient Rewrite button still looks ready to tap. In Translate, Close uses the primary gradient, so the main visual action is to give up.

Proposed fix

One plain message with what still works and what to do. Show Rewrite as disabled. Use a quiet secondary style for Close / Back to keyboard.

A2High

A rewrite failed silently: the panel closed and nothing changed

What happens

The very first Grammar fix on the phone closed the panel within a second. No result, no error, text unchanged. A later Grammar fix on a different sentence worked. Users who hit this once will assume AI doesn't work.

Proposed fix

Never close the panel without either a result or a visible error with Try again. Worth checking the logs for this case (first request after opening the panel).

A3Medium

The chosen style isn't remembered

What happens

After using Professional, reopening the panel selected Grammar fix again. People who usually want one tone have to pick it every time.

Proposed fix

Remember the last used style per user, or let them set a default style.

A4Medium

A ✅ emoji appears on the Grammar fix chip after use

What happens

Once Grammar fix has run, its chip shows a green ✅, which looks like "done" or "selected" next to the real selected chip with a ✓. Other styles show their own emoji (🙏, 💼).

Proposed fix

Use one consistent selected style, and pick an icon for Grammar fix that can't be read as a status.

A5High

No undo after Replace

What happens

Replace swaps the user's text for the AI version and the panel closes. Nothing says it happened and there is no undo, so if the AI dropped something (here "hey" disappeared) the user has to retype it.

Proposed fix

Show "Replaced with Professional · Undo" in the suggestion row for a few seconds (see sketch).

A6Low

Results are good and fast; make the comparison clearer

What happens

Results came back in about 2–4 seconds with a clear skeleton while loading, Show changes, Copy and Replace. Translate worked in under 2 seconds. The original text is hidden once the result appears, so it's hard to compare.

Proposed fix

Keep the original visible (collapsed) above the result. In the language list, show recent languages first and add search; for this user base, Hindi and other Indian languages near the top.

A7Low

Result is lost if the screen locks while loading

What happens

A Professional rewrite was still loading when the phone locked. After unlocking, the result was gone and the request had been spent.

Proposed fix

Keep the last result for a short time and show it again when the keyboard reopens on the same text.

A8Highneeds check

Keyboard panels may be invisible to screen readers

What happens

Android's accessibility tree did not expose the AI panel, Translate panel or their buttons (Rewrite, Copy, Replace, Close). If TalkBack can't see them, blind and low-vision users can't use AI at all.

Proposed fix

Test the AI and Translate panels with TalkBack. Give every action a content description and make the panels reachable by accessibility focus.

A9High

System Back on the AI panel closes the whole keyboard

What happens

With the AI panel open, the Android Back gesture hides the keyboard completely instead of returning to the letter keys. To keep typing, the user has to tap the text box again and the AI panel state is lost.

Proposed fix

Back from any keyboard panel (AI, Translate, Clipboard, Emoji, More) returns to the letter keys. Only Back from the letter keys hides the keyboard.

A10Medium

The panel's back button looks like the Enter key

What happens

The only in-panel way back is a small ↵ arrow at the top left. It's the same shape as Enter, sits far from where the thumb is, and has no label. Users told us this feels wrong.

Proposed fix

Replace it with a keyboard icon labelled "ABC" in the bottom-left corner, where the ?123 key normally is, so going back is the same gesture as switching layouts.

A11Medium

The AI panel repeats text the user can already see

What happens

The panel shows the full sentence in a quote box right under the text field that already shows it. It uses a third of the panel and pushes styles and the Rewrite button down.

Proposed fix

Drop the quote box. Show a one-line scope chip instead ("Whole message · 6 words" or "Selection · 3 words") so users know what will be rewritten. Use the freed space to show the result in place.

Languages

Adding and switching keyboard languages.

L1High

Languages list says "No keyboard languages yet" while English works

What happens

On a fresh install, the keyboard types in English, but the list is empty and says "Add a language to start using SmarType".

Proposed fix

Show the language that's actually in use (English, QWERTY) as the first row from the start.

L2High

Adding Hindi silently removes English, and the globe key leaves SmarType

What happens

After adding Hindi (India), the keyboard switched to Devanagari only and English was gone from the list. The globe key then opened another installed keyboard instead of switching SmarType back to English. Users are stuck until they find Settings → Languages and add English again.

Proposed fix

Adding a language adds it; it never removes the current one. The globe key (and a long-press on space) cycles SmarType's own languages first and only offers other keyboards after that.

L3Medium

"Suggested" languages are dozens of English regional variants

What happens

The suggestions start with English, English (American Samoa), English (Anguilla), English (Antigua & Barbuda)… Users in India have to search to find Hindi or any Indian language.

Proposed fix

Suggest the device's languages plus the region's common ones (for India: Hindi, Hinglish, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali…). Collapse English variants under one English row with a region picker.

L4Medium

No layout choice, reorder or default; jargon in the help text

What happens

Rows can't be tapped, so there's no way to choose a layout (for example Hindi on QWERTY with transliteration, which most Hindi typists use), set a default or change the order. The helper text mentions an "advanced subtype configuration" that users can't find.

Proposed fix

Make each row open a detail sheet: layout (Devanagari, Transliteration on QWERTY), set as default, remove. Allow drag to reorder. Rewrite the helper text in plain words.

L5Low

English suggestions appear on the Hindi layout

What happens

With the Hindi layout active, the suggestion row kept offering English words for the existing English text.

Proposed fix

Suggestions should follow the active language, or show both when the user mixes languages on purpose.

Quick Notes

The scratchpad and saved notes.

N1Medium

Five names for one feature

What happens

The same feature is called Quick Notes, Floating Quick Note, scratchpad, Quick Note, Scratch draft, New draft and Notes, depending on the screen.

Proposed fix

Pick one name and use it everywhere (see the Write space proposal below).

N2Medium

"Saved" shows while typing; Save clears the editor

What happens

The header says "Saved" before anything is saved. Tapping Save empties the editor, so it looks like the note disappeared; it's only visible in the list behind the ≡ icon. Saved notes show the first line twice (title and preview).

Proposed fix

Autosave with an honest status ("Saving…" / "Saved 11:31"). Keep the note open after saving. Show the first line as the title and the next line as the preview.

N3Medium

Notes can't be copied, shared or improved with AI

What happens

The note editor has no Copy, Share or Rewrite. The usual job (draft a message, then paste it into another app) needs long-press, select all and copy.

Proposed fix

Add a bottom action bar: Copy, Share, AI rewrite, and Paste into the app you came from.

Dictation

The mic button on the keyboard toolbar.

D1High

The mic hands the user to Google's keyboard; voice and AI are two separate jobs

What happens

SmarType has no voice input of its own. The mic key switches the whole keyboard to Google voice typing: different look, Google branding, no SmarType toolbar, styles or AI. After about 3 seconds of silence it stops with "Didn't catch that. Try speaking again." To get clean text the user has to dictate, tap ← to come back to SmarType, open the AI panel and rewrite: four steps for one message. On the phone ← returned to SmarType; on the emulator Google voice typing stayed the active keyboard even after a restart.

Proposed fix

Build SmarType's own voice mode inside the keyboard and drop the hand-off to Google: speech, clean-up and an optional writing style in one flow (see the proposal below). Short term, until that ships: label the mic clearly and make sure every exit returns to SmarType.

D2High

Google voice typing: about 1 error in 10 words, no punctuation

What happens

On the Galaxy S22 Ultra (Google on-device speech model), the owner dictated about 60 words with natural pauses. It kept listening through the pauses, but produced one run-on sentence with no punctuation or capitals and about 6 misheard phrases: "addictation" (a dictation), "it use the study fault" (it uses the default), "I am a zooming" (I am assuming), "it is an type" (it is not typing), "aiv ride" (AI rewrite). The Hindi word "hai" was kept in Latin script.

Proposed fix

This is the gap the SmarType dictation proposal targets: a clean-up pass after recognition (punctuation, sentences, fixing likely mishearings from context, product words like "AI rewrite"), and a choice between exact words and cleaned text.

Look and display

Dark mode, large text and landscape.

V1Medium

In dark mode the keyboard stays light; Upgrade text loses contrast

What happens

With the system in dark mode and Themes set to Day & night, the keyboard stayed on the light SmarType Day theme. On Home, the grey "Upgrade to Premium" label on the bright gradient is hard to read in dark mode.

Proposed fix

Check that Day & night follows the system theme by default. Give the gradient button its own tested text colour in both themes.

V2High

"Sign in before restoring" toast appears on every launch

What happens

This is not only right after sign-in (O4): a signed-in user saw it again on a cold start.

Proposed fix

Only show this message when a signed-out user taps Restore or Buy.

V3Low

Landscape keyboard leaves one line for the text; emoji button appears twice

What happens

In landscape the keyboard takes about 80% of the screen. The emoji button is in the toolbar and on the bottom row in every orientation. Large text (1.5×) worked well: text wraps and nothing is cut off.

Proposed fix

Use a shorter key height in landscape (or offer a split layout). Remove one of the two emoji buttons.

V4Low

Small copy issues in Account and Writing styles

What happens

Account says "Google sign-in with Firebase" and shows Sign Out as a large red button. Writing styles says "Tap Add style to start" but there is no Add style button. The keyboard icon in the "Try" box does nothing; only tapping the text opens the keyboard.

Proposed fix

Say "Signed in with Google". Make Sign Out a quieter row. Add the missing Add style button. Make the keyboard icon open the keyboard.

AI settings and writing styles

AS1Medium

Personal providers card contradicts itself

What happens

The card says "Your key, encrypted on device" and the line underneath says "Key stays on the server". The feature is also marked Coming soon, so the card takes space for something the user can't use.

Proposed fix

Hide Personal providers until it ships. Make the privacy line describe what actually happens today in one sentence.

AS2Low

SmarType AI page says Premium twice and nothing else

What happens

A large Premium hero is followed by a Premium card ("Unlimited SmarType AI") and the signed-in account. There's no usage, renewal date or link to manage the plan.

Proposed fix

Merge the hero and card into one block with the renewal date and a Manage link. For free users, show remaining free rewrites here.

AS3Medium

Writing styles shows 23 chips at once; the 4-pin limit isn't explained

What happens

"Your keyboard row" lists every style as chips, with no hint whether tapping one does anything. Below, "Pinned · 4 of 4, shown first" hints at a limit without saying it is a limit or how to swap.

Proposed fix

Lead with the 4 pinned styles ("On your keyboard, 4 max") and drag to reorder. Group the rest (Everyday, Work, Fun) with a clear Pin action.

Subscription

P1Highemulator

"Sign in before loading the billing catalog" shown to a signed-in user

What happens

The user is signed in, yet the page says to sign in. "Billing catalog" is an internal term. The only action, Retry plans, keeps failing because the real cause (device verification) isn't something a retry fixes.

Proposed fix

Show the real reason in plain words and hide Retry when it can't help. Example: "Plans can't load on this device because Google Play couldn't confirm it."

P2Mediumemulatorneeds check

Back from the subscription page left SmarType

What happens

Pressing Back on Premium Subscriptions opened the Play Store's home instead of returning to SmarType Home.

Proposed fix

Check the back stack when the subscription page is opened from Home, especially after a failed plan load.

P3Mediumemulatorneeds check

Reopening the app showed a blank screen, then closed

What happens

After the subscription error, relaunching SmarType showed an empty screen for several seconds and then returned to the Android home screen. Opening it again from the icon worked. No crash was logged.

Proposed fix

Check cold-start after a failed plan load; show the launch screen until Home is ready.

New features

Three proposals

Detailed specs for proposals 2 and 3: SmarType Write and Voice Specs.

These go beyond fixes. Each needs a product decision and, for the AI and dictation parts, the owner's plan review (typed-text privacy and the managed AI quota are risky areas in this repo).

1. AI inside the keyboard, not on top of it

Today the AI panel replaces the keys, repeats the text and hides the way back (A9–A11).

  • Style chips appear in the suggestion row; the letter keys stay visible.
  • The result shows as a preview strip above the keys, with Replace, Copy, Try again.
  • Back, or the ABC key, always returns to the letters.
  • A scope chip says what will change: whole message or selection.

2. Write: Quick Notes and a playground in one place

One screen for drafting anything (an email, a reply, a post), polishing it with AI, then copying or sharing it. Saved drafts live in the same place.

  • A Write tab on Home opens a full-screen editor with SmarType's keyboard.
  • Start from a blank page or a template (Email, Reply, Message, Post).
  • Bottom bar: Rewrite, Translate, Dictate, Copy, Share.
  • Autosave to Drafts; the floating bubble opens the same editor over any app.
  • Replaces Quick Notes, scratchpad and the various "Try out" boxes.

3. SmarType dictation

Today the mic hands off to Google voice typing (D1), which gives up after a short pause and adds no punctuation (D2). Then the user has to open the AI panel and rewrite as a separate step. The goal is one flow: speak, and get finished text in your chosen style.

  • Keeps listening through pauses. The user stops it with a tap, or after a long silence they choose (say 5 s).
  • Live draft, then clean-up. Words appear as you speak; when you stop, SmarType tidies the whole thing: punctuation, filler words removed, false starts fixed ("Tuesday, no, Wednesday" → "Wednesday").
  • Three outputs: Exact words · Cleaned up · In a style (Professional, Casual…).
  • Mixed languages: Hindi and English in one sentence (Hinglish), typed in Latin or Devanagari script.
  • Voice commands: "new line", "delete that", "send".
  • Privacy: on-device recognition first; the clean-up step uses SmarType AI only when the user turns it on, with the same quota rules as rewrite.

Dictation: build notes for the team

PieceOptionsTrade-off
Speech to textAndroid SpeechRecognizer with on-device models (Android 13+); or an on-device Whisper model (whisper.cpp); or a server model through FunctionsThe Android recogniser is free and private but ends on silence, so it needs restarting across pauses. Whisper handles pauses and Hinglish better but adds 40–150 MB and battery cost. A server model is the most accurate but sends audio off the phone.
Pause handlingVoice-activity detection plus stitching consecutive segments into one draftThe key to "even if I pause, it understands": treat silence as a gap, not the end.
Clean-upA new managed task in Functions ("clean dictation"), next to rewrite and translateReuses the existing quota, App Check and privacy model. Audio never leaves the phone, only the text.
Where it runsInside the keyboard (mic key) and in the Write screenNeeds the record-audio permission, requested the first time with a clear explanation.
Success measureFewer manual edits after dictating; share of messages sent without changesTrack counts only. Never log audio or text.

On the emulator, AI and subscriptions fail the Play Integrity check, so findings marked emulator show error states that real users only see when verification fails (for example on rooted, custom-ROM or uncertified devices). They are still real screens users can reach.
